question: Should OpenClaw accept `includeFamily` as the opt-in Gateway/tool contract for reading reset-family transcript history, including rejecting `includeFamily` with `offset`?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but the durable API name, pagination semantics, and archived transcript visibility boundary are product/security decisions for maintainers.

options.title: Accept `includeFamily` contract
options.body: Merge after owner review accepts the opt-in selector, bounded reads, header checks, active-only default, and offset rejection as the supported contract.

options.title: Narrow or rename first
options.body: Ask the contributor to change the public selector or response semantics if maintainers want a different archive-history API shape.

options.title: Defer to broader archive design
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want reset-family history exposed only through a future export or archive-management surface.

recommendation.title: Accept `includeFamily` contract
recommendation.body: Merge after owner review accepts the opt-in selector, bounded reads, header checks, active-only default, and offset rejection as the supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice directly intersects the recent `sessions_history` pagination contract and the new `includeFamily` plus `offset` incompatibility.
